chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mutamattiʿ who shaved his head in Makkah. He said: If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him. If he did that deliberately in the first of the months for hajj, thirty days before, then there is nothing upon him. But if he did it deliberately after the thirty days in which hair is left to grow for hajj, then a blood-sacrifice is upon him, which he must shed.

key_terms.الشَّعْرُ: the hair grown for the rites of hajj
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: acting out of ignorance of the ruling
key_terms.دَمًا: a sacrificial blood-offering due as expiation
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: he sheds it, meaning he offers the sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamattiʿ who shaves his head in Makkah before hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ who shaves his head in Makkah instead of merely shortening the hair. It distinguishes between ignorance and deliberate action, and also between shaving before and after the thirty-day period in which the hair is left to grow for hajj. If done deliberately after that period, a blood-sacrifice becomes obligatory.
